findings.evidence: Symmetries.lean:178 `∀ h s z Q2, D (τ h) (Species.conj s) z Q2 = D h s z Q2` vs 192 `∀ h s z Q2, D (τ h) (Species.map ρ s) z Q2 = D h s z Q2`; Basic.lean:151 `comap τ σ D = fun h i => D (τ h) (σ i)`.
findings.fix: Define one predicate, e.g. `def Invariant (τ : Hadron → Hadron) (σ : Species Flavor → Species Flavor) (D) : Prop := comap τ σ D = D`, and keep the physics names as instances: `ChargeConjRelation τ D := Invariant τ Species.conj D`, `FlavorRelation τ ρ D := Invariant τ (Species.map ρ) D`. `ChargeConjRelation.apply_eq` (181) then generalises to `Involutive σ → Invariant τ σ D → D (τ h) s = D h (σ s)`, and `apply_map_eq_apply_conj` (216) to `Involutive τ → Invariant τ σ D → Invariant τ σ' D → D h (σ' s) = D h (σ s)`.
findings.issue: `ChargeConjRelation τ D` (line 177) and `FlavorRelation τ ρ D` (line 190) are one notion at two species maps: both unfold to `∀ h s z Q2, D (τ h) (σ s) z Q2 = D h s z Q2`, i.e. `comap τ σ D = D` for the `comap` added in this PR (Basic.lean:149). The species-conjugation map is hard-coded, although roadmap §0.4 bullet 1 asks for it "as explicit data".

findings.evidence: Both proofs are `intro h s z Q2; by_cases hz ...; by_cases hs ...` with the identical four `valenceStepFrag_apply_of_*` rewrites; the required instance holds since `C.mem_valence_conj h (Species.conj s) : Species.conj s ∈ valence (conj h) ↔ Species.conj (Species.conj s) ∈ valence h` (Symmetries.lean:111-113).
findings.fix: State it once for a general species map σ: `invariant_valenceStepFrag (hv : ∀ h s, σ s ∈ C.valence (τ h) ↔ s ∈ C.valence h) : Invariant τ σ (valenceStepFrag C)`, then derive the charge-conjugation case by instantiating `σ := Species.conj`, `τ := C.conj` with `C.mem_valence_conj` at `conj s` plus `Species.conj_conj`.
findings.issue: `chargeConjRelation_valenceStepFrag` (457-467) duplicates `flavorRelation_valenceStepFrag` (470-480) line for line; the latter's hypothesis `∀ h s, Species.map ρ s ∈ C.valence (τ h) ↔ s ∈ C.valence h` is already the general compatibility condition, and only the species map differs.

findings.evidence: Symmetries.lean:334-338 takes `hq : quark i ∈ C.valence h`, `hq' : antiquark i ∉ C.valence h`; Symmetries.lean:610 `favoured_pion_plus_down` is the antiquark-valence case.
findings.fix: Add the companion under `(hq' : Species.antiquark i ∈ C.valence h) (hq : Species.quark i ∉ C.valence h)` giving `favoured - unfavoured = D h (antiquark i) - D h (quark i)`, derived from `favoured_eq_apply_antiquark`/`unfavoured_eq_apply_quark` exactly as the existing one.
findings.issue: `favoured_sub_unfavoured_eq` is given only for the quark-valence orientation, while all four `favoured/unfavoured_eq_apply_*` lemmas (270-330) are supplied in both. The PR description advertises it as the `IsValenceFlavor` consequence, but a flavour whose antiquark is the valence constituent — e.g. `π⁺` at the down flavour, which this file itself exhibits at `favoured_pion_plus_down` — has no such lemma.

findings.evidence: `grep -n comap EpsilonEridani/` returns only Basic.lean's own declarations, the PDF.comap material, and Symmetries.lean:198.
findings.fix: Make them pay for themselves — routing the two relations through `comap` (finding 1) uses the def, and `Assumptions.comap`/`zMoment_comap` specialise to the missing `Assumptions (partonConj D)` and `zMoment (partonConj D)` lemmas; otherwise drop the unused ones.
findings.issue: Of the new `comap` block, only `comap`/`comap_apply` are used anywhere (once, by `partonConj`, Symmetries.lean:198); `comap_id`, `comap_comap`, `comap_indicatorUnitInterval`, `zMoment_comap` and `Assumptions.comap` have no consumer in the repo, contrary to the PR description's "the three pullbacks the symmetry material needs are instances of it".

summary: The two symmetry relations are the same predicate (`comap τ σ D = D`) written twice at `σ = Species.conj` and `σ = Species.map ρ`, which forces a duplicated witness proof and keeps the `comap` abstraction this PR adds almost entirely unused; `favoured_sub_unfavoured_eq` is also stated in only one of the two valence orientations the file otherwise covers.
